newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Top Vietnam prosecutor faces corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Top Vietnam prosecutor faces corruption probe.

text.p: Vietnam said on Thursday it was investigating its former chief prosecutor over allegations of corruption following a decision by the National Assembly earlier this week to dismiss him.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Tran Quang Hoan told journalists at a news briefing that Le Thanh Dao had made mistakes.

"Mr Le Thanh Dao has made some mistakes and was involved in a business wrongdoing," he said. "Subsequently the National Assembly decided that he failed to be qualified as a leader of the People's Supreme Inspectorate."
Dao was replaced on Monday, and a new chief prosecutor Ha Manh Tri named in his place.
In an interview with the Tuoi Tre newspaper, Communist Party chief Do Muoi pointed to the case as an example of Hanoi's determination to crack down on graft at every level of the establishment.

"If there's enough evidence then let's prosecute. If guilt has been found let's have a trial, regardless of who the person is, which position they are in and whose relatives they are," Muoi was quoted as saying.
"I would like to repeat, anti-corruption measures are very necessary, very urgent. But we have talked a lot, discussed a lot. Let's do it, do it immediately!"
Corruption is endemic in Vietnam. The country was named by a Hong Kong-based business consultancy earlier this year as one of the most graft-ridden in Asia.
Hanoi says it recognises the gravity of the problem. Hoan said Vietnam hoped to introduce tough new anti-corruption legislation soon.
